svg.title: Unclaimed Property Search Entry Sequence
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-search-entry-sequence; chapter number: 1; title: Unclaimed Property Search Entry Sequence; subtitle: From dormancy clock to a free claim or a capped finder agreement; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Confirm Dormancy Has Run; value: Step 1; detail: Dormancy runs one year for payroll and three to five years for bank accounts; an empty search may only mean the property has not yet been reported to the state (Hoang Le CFP, EA).; step: 02; label: Sweep MissingMoney.com First; value: Step 2; detail: More than $70 billion sits in state custody and about one in seven Americans has a stake; the median claim is about $100 against a $2,080 average (Hoang Le; Money Missed).; step: 03; label: Search Every State Portal; value: Step 3; detail: Search each state where the owner lived or worked, including deceased relatives; Illinois traced 119 relatives back five generations on the $11 million Stancak estate (Money Missed).; step: 04; label: Check Federal Registries; value: Step 4; detail: State databases do not hold federal assets such as wages, pensions, FHA refunds, failed banks, or bankruptcy court funds, so one portal never proves a zero result (This Guy Knows Tech).; step: 05; label: File Free or Use a Capped Finder; value: Step 5; detail: Self-filing costs nothing; registered finders are commonly capped at 10% to 30%, and a legitimate locator never asks to be paid first. State payouts typically land in 16 to 120 days.; caption: Five-step entry sequence for locating custodial money before it is worked as a claim.; assumptions note: Step order follows the practitioner consensus on search entry points; dollar figures are attributed practitioner claims, not audited totals.; note: Attributed to Hoang Le CFP, EA, Real Estate Agent; Money Missed; This Guy Knows Tech; Money Making Juggernaut (Eric Richardson).

rect.title: step: 01; label: Confirm Dormancy Has Run; value: Step 1; detail: Dormancy runs one year for payroll and three to five years for bank accounts; an empty search may only mean the property has not yet been reported to the state (Hoang Le CFP, EA).
